t.3.14.1: Then, having gone to Pañcavaṭī, which was filled with many kinds of beasts of prey and deer, Rāma spoke to his brother Lakṣmaṇa of blazing splendor.
t.3.14.3: Let your gaze be cast all around this forest, for you are skilled; in which place would a hermitage for us be fitting?
t.3.14.2: We have come to this region, just as the great sage directed. This, gentle one, is the region of Pañcavaṭī, its woods all in blossom.
t.3.14.4: O Lakṣmaṇa, let such a place be looked for, with a body of water close at hand, where Vaidehī may take delight, and you and I as well.
t.3.14.5: A place where there is the charm of the forest and likewise the charm of the waters, and where firewood, flowers, kuśa grass and water may be close at hand.
t.3.14.6: Thus addressed by Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, with palms joined in reverence, spoke these words to Kākutstha in the presence of Sītā.
t.3.14.8: Greatly pleased by those words of Lakṣmaṇa, the greatly radiant one, after reflecting, chose a place endowed with every good quality.
t.3.14.7: I am wholly dependent on you, O Kākutstha, even were you to remain here a hundred years. You yourself tell me, 'Let it be built in this pleasing place.'
t.3.14.9: Having stepped onto that lovely spot for the work of building a hermitage, Rāma took Saumitri's two hands in his own hand and spoke to him.
t.3.14.10: This place is level and lovely, surrounded by flowering trees. Here, gentle one, you should build a hermitage in the proper manner.
t.3.14.11: Not far off can be seen this lovely lotus pond, adorned with lotuses, its lotuses shining like the sun and bearing a sweet fragrance.
t.3.14.12: Just as it was described by the sage Agastya, whose soul is purified, here is the lovely Godāvarī, surrounded by trees in full bloom.
t.3.14.14: O gentle one, the mountains are seen, lofty and lovely, full of many caves, echoing with the cries of peacocks and covered with trees in full blossom.
t.3.14.13: Teeming with swans and kāraṇḍava ducks and adorned with cakravāka birds, it lies neither too far nor too near, thronged by herds of deer.
t.3.14.15: In this golden region, streaked here and there with minerals of silver and copper, they shine like elephants adorned with lattice-like patterns of the finest designs.
t.3.14.16: They are adorned with sāla, palmyra and tamāla trees, with date palms, jackfruit and mango trees, with wild rice, timiśa and puṃnāga trees.
t.3.14.17: They are covered with mango, aśoka, tilaka, campaka and ketaka trees, and with all those various trees endowed with flowers, shrubs and creepers.
t.3.14.18: It is graced with sandalwood, syandana, nīpa, jackfruit and lakuca trees, and with dhava, aśvakarṇa, khadira, śamī, kiṃśuka and pāṭala trees.
t.3.14.20: Thus addressed by Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, the slayer of enemy heroes and possessed of exceedingly great strength, quickly built a hermitage for his brother.
t.3.14.19: This place is holy, this place is pure, this place abounds in deer and birds. Here we shall dwell, O Saumitri, together with this bird.
t.3.14.21: There he raised a very spacious and most beautiful hut of leaves, its walls of packed clay, with sturdy pillars, and its rafters made of long bamboos.
t.3.14.22: Then the glorious Lakṣmaṇa went to the river Godāvarī, bathed, and, gathering lotuses, came back again with fruits as well.
t.3.14.24: Seeing that pleasant hermitage built, Rāghava, together with Sītā, felt supreme joy in the leaf-hut.
t.3.14.23: Then, having made an offering of flowers and performed the rite of propitiation according to rule, he showed Rāma the hermitage he had built.
t.3.14.25: Then, greatly delighted, he embraced Lakṣmaṇa with both arms and spoke these words, exceedingly affectionate and deeply earnest.
t.3.14.26: I am pleased with you, O lord, for this great deed that you have done; it is for this reason that an embrace was owed to you, and so I have embraced you.
t.3.14.27: O Lakṣmaṇa, through you, a son who understands the heart, is grateful, and knows dharma, my righteous father has not passed away.
t.3.14.28: Having thus spoken to Lakṣmaṇa, Rāghava, the increaser of prosperity, self-controlled, dwelt happily in that region abounding in fruit.
t.3.14.29: Attended by Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa, that righteous-souled one dwelt there for some time, like an immortal in the world of heaven.
